note: Canonical answers to business questions either workflow may ask. Approved by the benchmark owner on 2026-11-14. Paste the answer text when a workflow asks, so both workflows receive identical text. Do not reveal hidden test details.

decisions.question: How do we tell a retry of the same checkout apart from a new, legitimate purchase?
decisions.answer: A retry is a resubmission of the same checkout attempt: the customer submits the checkout they were already on (for example re-posting the same checkout page after a timeout, a double-click, or the browser resending the request). Once an order has been placed successfully, starting checkout again with a newly filled basket is a new purchase, even if it contains exactly the same items and quantities.

decisions.topic: Outcome shown for a retried checkout
decisions.question: What should the customer see when they retry a checkout whose order was already created?
decisions.answer: They should not get an error and must not be charged twice. Showing the normal order confirmation (success page) for the existing order is the preferred outcome.

decisions.question: If the same checkout is submitted twice at the same moment (double-click, two tabs), what should happen?
decisions.answer: Exactly one order must be created. The other submission must not fail with a server error; it should end on a normal page (confirmation or basket).

decisions.topic: Failure before the order is saved
decisions.question: If checkout fails before the order is saved, should the customer be able to retry?
decisions.answer: Yes. Nothing should be lost: the basket stays as it was and a retry should place exactly one order.

decisions.topic: Failure after the order is saved but before the customer is told
decisions.question: If the order was saved but something failed afterwards (so the customer saw an error or a timeout), what should a retry do?
decisions.answer: The customer must end up with exactly one order for that checkout. Either the whole checkout succeeds or fails as a unit, or the retry recognises the order that already exists; both are acceptable.

decisions.question: Should we block a second order that has the same items as a recent order from the same customer?
decisions.answer: No. Customers legitimately reorder the same items, sometimes within minutes. Do not block or merge orders based on content or timing alone.

decisions.topic: Retry from a freshly reloaded checkout page
decisions.question: If the first submission is still processing and the customer reloads the checkout page and submits again, is that a retry or a new order?
decisions.answer: It is a retry of the same checkout. The first submission has not finished, so that basket has not been ordered yet; submitting it again from a reloaded checkout page must not create a second order. Only after an order has been placed does a newly filled basket count as a new purchase.

decisions.question: Which checkout entry points are in scope?
decisions.answer: The customer-facing web checkout (Basket > Checkout > Pay Now). There is no separate order-placing API today.

decisions.question: Are database schema changes acceptable?
decisions.answer: Yes, if they are delivered as an Entity Framework migration consistent with the existing migrations and the existing data remains valid.

decisions.question: For how long after the first attempt must a retry be recognised as the same checkout?
decisions.answer: At least for the time a customer could reasonably retry after a timeout: minutes to hours. Retries are expected within the same browser session.
